review_boundary: Artifact-only review of an additive local-only analysis preregistration. No provider, protected evaluator payload, measured retrieval, model, or external evidence was accessed.

overall.one_line_summary: V12 supplies a publication-grade analysis boundary for the unchanged v11 request without creating execution authority or treating development evidence as confirmation.
strengths: The contract immutably binds the v11 request and receipt by file and self SHA-256.
OUT Recall@100 remains the sole primary outcome and OUT nDCG@100/@10 remain ordered secondaries.
Candidate exposure, oracle diagnostics, complementarity, interaction scope, operational measurement, and confirmation statistics are separated explicitly.
Selection-125 is prohibited from serving as confirmation and Final-872 is designated the sole confirmatory evaluation.
weaknesses: The protected evaluator must still bind exact missing/unjudged handling, bootstrap seed, and final comparator identities before measured work.
No measured evidence exists; the contract cannot support a performance or publication claim by itself.

strengths: The outcome hierarchy distinguishes candidate exposure from ranking quality and binds the family-level OUT estimand.
suggestions: Keep oracle-pool diagnostics visually and semantically separate from deployed Recall@100 in later reports.

strengths: The primary superiority rule, paired unit, 10,000 resamples, CI interpretation, and no-max-cell rule are explicit.
weaknesses: The frozen confirmation receipt must provide the exact bootstrap seed and concrete comparator hashes.
suggestions: Fail the future confirmation package when either field is missing or differs from its frozen comparator bundle.

strengths: Interaction claims are explicitly limited to five frozen arms, five programs, DAPFAM, and the frozen budget; universal causal claims are forbidden.
The v11 binding, development-to-confirmation path, exposure controls, analysis outputs, and safe reporting form a traceable claim chain.
weaknesses: The later adoption/confirmation packages must reference this contract explicitly to make the future lineage mechanically complete.
suggestions: Bind this contract SHA-256 in the separate adoption receipt and final aggregate claim receipt.

strengths: REP-DEV and HARNESS-DEV are labelled exploratory; Selection-125 is one-time finalist selection, and post-exposure mutation is forbidden.
Equal total candidate depth, pool binding, unique-pair denominator, operational repetition policy, and paired effect reporting are preregistered.
weaknesses: Exact candidate promotion thresholds and the final protected evaluator's missing/unjudged policy remain deferred to future frozen receipts.
suggestions: Before the first measured screen, bind a replayable lexicographic promotion rule and the protected evaluator policy without exposing protected payloads.

findings.observation: V12 requires a replayable lexicographic promotion rule but intentionally does not freeze its numerical thresholds in this local-only layer.
findings.reasoning: This preserves the unchanged v11 request but leaves a required future binding before any candidate result is evaluated.
findings.suggestion: Add the threshold-bearing promotion receipt before the first measured A1.2 result and bind its SHA-256 into adoption lineage.
